evidence.quote: Abundant dislocations were found to form dislocation networks, and there was an angle of 80 degrees between the double-slip bands, as shown in Figure 8b.

evidence.section: 3.4. Microstructures of the Annealed Ti3VNbAl0.5Zrx Alloys After Tensile Deformation
evidence.quote: In Figure 8c, the Taylor lattices are clearly visible. The Taylor lattice represents an arrangement of low-energy dislocation structures, and its presence is indicative of the dissipation of deformation energy.

evidence.section: 3.4. Microstructures of the Annealed Ti3VNbAl0.5Zrx Alloys After Tensile Deformation
evidence.quote: The Taylor lattice is composed of high-density dislocation walls (HDDWs), with regions of lower dislocation density surrounding these walls. HDDWs act as barriers to dislocation motion, causing localized dislocation accumulation and the development of complex tangles and loops.

evidence.section: 3.4. Microstructures of the Annealed Ti3VNbAl0.5Zrx Alloys After Tensile Deformation
evidence.quote: Figure 8d presents a large number of dislocation pile-ups near the grain boundary. Dislocation tangles, loops, and pile-ups collectively increase the resistance to dislocation movement, thereby stabilizing plastic deformation and enhancing the alloys’ yield strength

evidence.quote: Based on the results presented above, it can be concluded that dislocation slip is the main deformation mechanism of the Zr1 alloy, and dislocation interactions are key to achieving superior strength–ductility synergy.
